common_name: Atom Smasher Hosta (Ruffled Gold Breeding-Line Mini Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Atom Smasher is a small mini hosta bred by Ron Livingston from a cross of 'Ginko Craig' and 'Chartreuse Wiggles', valued by hybridizers as a prolific breeding parent as much as a garden plant in its own right. Narrow, lance-shaped bright yellow leaves carry an extreme, heavily ruffled margin that gives the small mound a frilled, almost wind-blown look even in still air. Lavender flowers rise on short scapes in summer and are followed by showy red seed pods that extend its season of interest. Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where a little morning sun helps hold the gold color.

common_name: Little Jim Hosta (Streaked Mini Sport of Saishu Jima)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Little Jim is Herb Benedict's 1986 sport of 'Saishu Jima', inheriting its parent's narrow, lance-shaped leaves but trading a simpler pattern for irregular, unstable streaks of green, gold, and white that vary from leaf to leaf and even season to season. Pale purple, lightly striped flowers rise above the small mound in summer. Plants multiply quickly for a variegated mini hosta and frequently throw additional variegated seedlings when allowed to self-sow. Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, dividing clumps in spring as they fill in.

common_name: Blaze of Glory Hosta (Vivid Gold Pin Stripe Seedling)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Blaze of Glory is Ed Elslager's 1999-registered seedling of 'Pin Stripe', grown for leaves that open a brilliant, almost lemony light yellow in spring before settling to a slightly greener gold through summer. The rounded, lightly corrugated leaves have good substance and a wavy margin, and near-white, lightly fragrant flowers appear on tall scapes in July. It builds into a large, vigorous mound over a few seasons, living up to its name as one of the most vivid gold hostas in cultivation. Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where some morning sun intensifies the gold color without scorching the leaves.
